Needs changes before merge. One finding.

**Requested before merge**

1. **P3 — Name the grazing plunge on tabbed helix levels.** [crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_step.rs:132](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/50389b330d78d50079ccc9381820394b352d16db/crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_step.rs#L132).

   The first successful helix ramp sets `said.refused` at line 128. Later tabbed levels then skip the note at line 132. Their entry note still says that the helix uses a ramp, although these levels plunge.

   I reproduced this with these parameters:

   - Part: 30 × 30 mm; tool: Ø10 mm; side: Outside; lead: None.
   - Top Z: 0; Bottom Z: -3; stepdown: 1 mm.
   - Entry: Helix; approach ramp angle: 5 degrees; helix radius: 3 mm.
   - Two tabs; width: 5 mm; height: 1.5 mm; links: `Links::PLANAR`.

   Result: four `Plunge` moves. The only entry note says:

   ```text
   entry: the helix needs bounded air only a bore (Side::Inside) has - ramp along the lead-in and the ring instead
   ```

   The same setup with Entry Ramp includes the standing-tab reason. Issue #3829 and this PR both require that reason for the graze.

   Track the helix substitution and the graze refusal separately. Add a regression test with untabbed and tabbed helix levels. Require both notes, each once.

**Local validation**

Merging as SAME (no head movement since the counted review). The review that stands: `<!-- pr-reviewer: 5dbc96b21b42be2840762d4aca675c408f856caf -->` by mkinney, clean at head `5dbc96b21b42be2840762d4aca675c408f856caf`. Merge commit pinned with `--match-head-commit`.

Post-merge safety review (read-only, on origin/main after 2e2d40cb3). Nothing was built or run.

1. **No gouge of the part wall: one defect, filed as #3888 (P1).**
   - Without compensation the result is correct. `contour_wall_ramp.rs` lines 45-47 put every zig-zag point on the lead-in or the centre ring. The centre ring is one tool radius plus the stock to leave off the part. No point is inside the part.
   - With control or wear compensation the zig-zag legs run on the ring before G41/G42 engages. G41/G42 engages on the lead-in move (`contour.rs` lines 336-348, `contour_comp.rs` lines 172-178). The ramp moves thus do not get the register value. A register larger than the nominal radius, or a positive wear value, cuts the wall. `contour_comp::door` does not refuse this combination.
2. **Descent: correct.** On later levels the ramp starts at `prev_z`, on the path that the level above cut, so it is in air (`contour_wall_ramp.rs` lines 34-37). On the first level it is a ramp entry at the stated angle from the top of the cut plus the plunge height. A path that is too short or a tabbed level gives the graze and a note (`contour_step.rs` lines 127-143). The graze keeps the centre-cut refusal (`contour_step.rs` lines 157-169).
3. **Ramp angle: correct for the operation angle. No issue filed.**
   - `push_zig` (`links.rs`) descends linearly in path length. Each leg is no steeper than `ramp_angle`, or the 3 deg default (`contour_wall_ramp.rs` lines 38-44).
   - The tool has no maximum ramp angle field in this repository. A tool that is not centre-cutting ramps at any angle that the user sets (below 90 deg). This agrees with the bore side (`contour_bore.rs` lines 124-133) and the pass links (`contour_link.rs` line 250).
4. **Stock to leave, levels and last pass: correct.** The zig-zag runs on the centre ring, which includes the stock to leave, and ends at the lead-in start at `s.z`. Each level then cuts the full lead-in and ring at `s.z`. No ramp point goes past the final wall, and no ramp stops above the level.
5. **No panic: correct.** `wall_ramp` has no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic`. `plan_zig_capped` returns `None` on a short path, a non-finite number or more than `MAX_ZIG_LEGS` legs. The caller then grazes with a note. A closed ring and the arcs of a sharp corner are flattened, and the ramp stays on them. A minor point: when `ramp_max_len` caps the legs, the note says "too short for the ramp angle" and does not name the maximum length.
6. **Tests:**
   - `a_wall_side_ramp_entry_ramps_every_level_within_its_angle` pins points 1 and 2 (no axial dive, at most 5 deg, the centre stays one radius off the part). It fails without the fix, because the old graze has an axial dive.
   - `a_wall_side_ramp_too_short_for_its_angle_grazes_and_says_why` and `a_wall_side_helix_names_its_ramp_and_its_tabbed_graze_each_once` pin point 5. They fail without the fix (new note text).
   - No test covers compensation (#3888) or a tool that is not centre-cutting.

Issues filed: #3888 (P1, effort:high).
